subtopic: Moving to a new city for study
subtype: Approach: leaning on new friends without checking their advice [Pitfall]
passage: I'm Mohit. In my second week in the city, my senior Rafiq told me about a coaching centre near the station: cheap fees, small batches, results guaranteed. “Trust me, bhai, everyone from our floor goes.” I was new and didn't want to look stupid, so I paid the whole term's fees in cash, told myself Papa would approve, and didn't ask him. I never looked at the registration or asked anyone else. Six weeks later I reached the door and found a lock and a torn notice. The fees were gone. Rafiq was as shocked as I was. Looking back, the mistake wasn't trusting a friend; it was skipping the two easy checks, asking my parents and finding out whether the centre was registered.

qa.q: What did Mohit find at the coaching centre six weeks later?
qa.a: Mohit found a lock and a torn notice.

qa.q: Why did Mohit pay the fees in cash without asking anyone?
qa.a: Mohit was new and afraid of looking stupid, so the wish to fit in mattered more than checking.

qa.q: What could Mohit do before paying for a course next time?
qa.a: Mohit could ask his parents and find out whether the centre is registered, since these two easy checks expose a doubtful offer.

qa.q: How might Rafiq have felt when the centre closed?
qa.a: Rafiq was as shocked as Mohit, so probably embarrassed and sorry that the tip led to a loss.

grounding: A newcomer follows a senior's tip for a cheap unregistered coaching centre without asking parents or checking, and loses the fees when it closes.

subtopic: Moving to a new city for study
subtype: Approach: leaning on new friends without checking their advice [Pitfall]
passage:
Warden's note, hostel office, 14 November
Mohit, Room 22, came to see me today very upset. In August a senior, Lalit, told him about a cheap coaching centre above a shop near the market: half the price of the big institutes, “same teachers”. Mohit paid the term's fees in cash the same week. He did not tell his parents first or ask the college office about it, because Lalit seemed to know everything.
Yesterday the centre's shutter was down, with a paper sign. The phone is off. Four other students from this hostel also paid.
I sat with Mohit while he called his father, and we have noted the centre's details for a police complaint, which his father will file with him on Saturday. I have also put up a notice: before paying any coaching centre, check with the college office and tell your family.

qa.q: How many other students from the hostel also paid?
How was Mohit feeling when he came to the warden?
qa.a: Mohit was very upset, probably ashamed of trusting too quickly and worried about telling his father.

qa.q: What simple checks could Mohit have made in August?
qa.a: Ask the college office whether the centre was known and registered, and talk it over with his parents before paying.
Lalit may feel guilty and embarrassed that such a confident tip cost Mohit and others.

grounding: A warden notes a newcomer who followed a senior's tip for a cheap unregistered coaching centre without checking, and lost the fees when it closed.

subtopic: Moving to a new city for study
subtype: Approach: leaning on new friends without checking their advice [Pitfall]
passage:
Saturday
Writing this down so I never forget how foolish I feel.
When I moved here in July, Gargi Didi from the top floor said the best-value test series in the city was at a small centre near the station. “Everyone goes,” she said. “Pay for the full year, it's cheaper.” She was so friendly and sure, and I wanted to seem like I knew what I was doing. So I paid for the whole year from the money Papa sent for books and fees, without telling him first.
Today I went for the Saturday test and the door had a lock on it. A neighbour said they shut last week and nobody knows where the owner went. There's no registration board, and no receipt with an address.
I called Papa tonight and told him everything. He was quiet, then said, “Next time, we check together first. Tomorrow we go to the police station.”
Gargi Didi says she didn't know.
– Mohit

qa.q: What did Mohit find at the centre on Saturday?
qa.a: The door had a lock on it.

qa.q: Why did Mohit pay without checking?
qa.a: Mohit wanted to seem like someone who knew what to do, and Gargi Didi's friendly certainty felt reassuring.

qa.q: What simple checks could Mohit have made in July?
qa.a: Look for a registration and a proper receipt with an address, ask the college office, and talk to Papa before paying.

qa.q: How might Papa feel hearing this?
qa.a: Papa is probably upset and worried, but steady, focusing on checking together next time and going to the police.

grounding: Shows a newcomer following a senior's advice to pay a cheap, unregistered centre without checking, and losing the fees when it shuts.
